From c842743d073bdd683606cb414eb0ca84465dd834 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ruide Cao <caoruide123@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 22:46:20 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] net: sched: act_csum: validate nested VLAN headers

tcf_csum_act() walks nested VLAN headers directly from skb->data when an
skb still carries in-payload VLAN tags. The current code reads
vlan->h_vlan_encapsulated_proto and then pulls VLAN_HLEN bytes without
first ensuring that the full VLAN header is present in the linear area.

If only part of an inner VLAN header is linearized, accessing
h_vlan_encapsulated_proto reads past the linear area, and the following
skb_pull(VLAN_HLEN) may violate skb invariants.

Fix this by requiring pskb_may_pull(skb, VLAN_HLEN) before accessing and
pulling each nested VLAN header. If the header still is not fully
available, drop the packet through the existing error path.

Fixes: 2ecba2d1e45b ("net: sched: act_csum: Fix csum calc for tagged packets")
Reported-by: Yifan Wu <yifanwucs@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Juefei Pu <tomapufckgml@gmail.com>
Co-developed-by: Yuan Tan <yuantan098@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Yuan Tan <yuantan098@gmail.com>
Suggested-by: Xin Liu <bird@lzu.edu.cn>
Tested-by: Ren Wei <enjou1224z@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Ruide Cao <caoruide123@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Ren Wei <n05ec@lzu.edu.cn>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/22df2fcb49f410203eafa5d97963dd36089f4ecf.1774892775.git.caoruide123@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/sched/act_csum.c b/net/sched/act_csum.c
index 213e1ce9d2da..a9e4635d899e 100644
--- a/net/sched/act_csum.c
+++ b/net/sched/act_csum.c
@@ -604,8 +604,12 @@ TC_INDIRECT_SCOPE int tcf_csum_act(struct sk_buff *skb,
 			protocol = skb->protocol;
 			orig_vlan_tag_present = true;
 		} else {
-			struct vlan_hdr *vlan = (struct vlan_hdr *)skb->data;
+			struct vlan_hdr *vlan;
 
+			if (!pskb_may_pull(skb, VLAN_HLEN))
+				goto drop;
+
+			vlan = (struct vlan_hdr *)skb->data;
 			protocol = vlan->h_vlan_encapsulated_proto;
 			skb_pull(skb, VLAN_HLEN);
 			skb_reset_network_header(skb);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `net/sched/act_csum.c`

**Change**:  
In function `tcf_csum_act()`, within the `else` branch that processes a nested (inner) VLAN header (when the skb still carries in-payload VLAN tags), the code now:

1. **Adds a safety check** using `pskb_may_pull(skb, VLAN_HLEN)` before dereferencing the VLAN header pointer.
2. **Moves the declaration** of `struct vlan_hdr *vlan` from the original cast-and-access location to after the `pskb_may_pull` check, ensuring the pointer is only set once the header is guaranteed to be fully linear.
3. If the pull check fails, the packet is dropped via the existing `goto drop` path.

**Reason**:  
Previously, the code read `vlan->h_vlan_encapsulated_proto` and then called `skb_pull(skb, VLAN_HLEN)` without first verifying that the entire VLAN header was in the linear area of the skb. This could cause out-of-bounds reads and violate skb invariants when only part of the inner VLAN header was linearized.

### Relationships Between Changes

- The modification is confined to a single conditional block within a single file.
- The added `pskb_may_pull` check directly addresses the root cause of the vulnerability: it ensures the necessary data is present in linear memory before any access or pull operation.
- Moving the variable declaration after the check is a logical consequence of the new ordering—the pointer must not be set until the data is confirmed to be available.
- The `goto drop` path was already present, so the fix integrates seamlessly with the existing error handling.
